triage.instructions: An open issue has not been turned into a swarm work card. Decide what kind of work it is. The three tree facts in the state -- held_by_open_pr, cited_path_exists_on_dev, last_comment_says_fixed -- are computed by the asker before this question is asked, because you cannot see the tree and guessing about it is what made this question wrong before. Answer from the state's fields; docs/decide/criteria-triage.md is the long form and the asker embeds it above.

criteria.mechanical-card: ALL of: the issue names exact PATHS or a red test that exists; the repair is one line, one flag, one count or one refusal with no door; acceptance is a single sentence; no design ruling is needed; held_by_open_pr=no; cited_path_exists_on_dev=yes; last_comment_says_fixed=no. A capable small model writes it from a card with anchors, red test first.
criteria.design-ruling: The issue asks a question rather than reporting a defect: which of two shapes, whether a behaviour should exist, what a specification ought to say, what number a bound takes. A card cannot pick the number.
criteria.already-fixed: last_comment_says_fixed=yes, or issue_state is closed, or cited_path_exists_on_dev=no because the code the issue describes is not on dev in that shape any more.
criteria.held: held_by_open_pr=yes. The repair is real and unheld work is not: an open pull request already touches the file, so a card would collide with it. This is not a judgement about the issue, it is a fact about the tree.
criteria.infra-opus: The work lives in the repository's own machinery rather than its tools: CI workflows, tools/ and scripts/, the swarm and pulse launchers, the sandbox, or anything touching keys, credentials or a destructive operation's guard.
